title: Drugs that lower the seizure threshold
scopeNotes: Labels and an FDA safety communication; Beers 2023 items apply to adults ≥65

entries.title: Bupropion
effect: Dose-related seizures: ~0.4% at up to 450 mg/day (IR label)
pearls: Contraindicated: seizure disorder; current or prior bulimia/anorexia; abrupt withdrawal of alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates or antiseizure medications
Other risk factors (label): severe head injury, AVM, CNS tumor or infection, severe stroke, metabolic disorders (hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, hypoxia), other threshold-lowering drugs
IR: max 450 mg/day, ≤150 mg per dose, titrate gradually; stop if a seizure occurs
SR and XL maximum doses differ from IR — not covered by the label on file
sources: Bupropion hydrochloride tablets US prescribing information. Cipla; revised 3/2023 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Flumazenil
effect: Seizures, most often after long-term benzodiazepine sedation or in overdose with serious cyclic antidepressant toxicity
pearls: Contraindicated when a benzodiazepine is controlling a life-threatening condition (e.g., ICP, status epilepticus) or with signs of serious cyclic antidepressant overdose
Precipitates withdrawal seizures in benzodiazepine-dependent patients
Not recommended to diagnose benzodiazepine sedation in the ICU
Watch for resedation after reversal
sources: Flumazenil injection US prescribing information. Akorn-Strides; revised 5/2008 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Cefepime
effect: Non-convulsive status epilepticus — FDA review: 59 cases, nearly all with renal impairment; 56 without renal dose adjustment
pearls: Mean onset ~6 days (range 1–15) in published cases; most recover after stopping cefepime ± antiseizure treatment
Unexplained confusion on cefepime, especially older or renally impaired: consider EEG
Dose to renal function per label and reassess as renal function changes
sources: FDA Drug Safety Communication on cefepime and non-convulsive status epilepticus (2012), as summarized in: Song JC. Cefepime: FDA Drug Safety Communication on non-convulsive status epilepticus risk. Infect Dis Alert 2012;31(11)

entries.title: Other beta-lactams and carbapenems
effect: Non-convulsive status epilepticus reported, including 8 published ceftazidime cases (onset 3–8 days, nearly all with renal impairment)
pearls: Risk factors for antibiotic-induced seizures: prior seizures, renal impairment, meningitis/CNS infection, extremes of age, low albumin
Carbapenems also lower valproate levels — see asm-interactions
sources: FDA Drug Safety Communication on cefepime and non-convulsive status epilepticus (2012), as summarized in: Song JC. Cefepime: FDA Drug Safety Communication on non-convulsive status epilepticus risk. Infect Dis Alert 2012;31(11)

entries.title: Fluoroquinolones
effect: Non-convulsive status epilepticus reported; ciprofloxacin raises CNS risk (seizures, confusion) when CrCl <30
pearls: Beers 2023 (adults ≥65): ciprofloxacin doses usually need reduction at CrCl <30 mL/min
Also on the MG caution list
sources: FDA Drug Safety Communication on cefepime and non-convulsive status epilepticus (2012), as summarized in: Song JC. Cefepime: FDA Drug Safety Communication on non-convulsive status epilepticus risk. Infect Dis Alert 2012;31(11)

2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc 2023;71:2052-2081. doi:10.1111/jgs.18372

entries.title: Theophylline
effect: Seizures with toxicity (often >30 mcg/mL); isolated seizures reported below 20 mcg/mL in older patients and those with neurologic disease
pearls: Label: extreme caution in seizure disorders
Toxicity seizures are hard to stop — benzodiazepines then phenobarbital; label calls for rapid, aggressive treatment
Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels — avoid the combination (Beers 2023)
Many conditions and drugs reduce clearance; label advises frequent serum concentrations in acutely ill patients
sources: Theophylline anhydrous extended-release tablets US prescribing information. Westminster; revised 12/2025 (user-supplied label)

2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc 2023;71:2052-2081. doi:10.1111/jgs.18372

entries.title: Clozapine
effect: Dose-related seizures: ~5% cumulative incidence at 1 year
pearls: Boxed warning includes seizure
Start 12.5 mg, titrate slowly, divided doses
Caution with prior seizures or risk factors (head trauma, CNS pathology, threshold-lowering drugs, alcohol use)
Counsel against driving, swimming or climbing
sources: Clozapine tablets US prescribing information. Accord; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Tramadol
effect: Seizures within the recommended dose range; risk rises above it
pearls: Higher risk with epilepsy or prior seizures, head trauma, metabolic disorders, alcohol/drug withdrawal, CNS infection
Risk rises with SSRIs, TCAs and tricyclic compounds (e.g., cyclobenzaprine), other opioids, MAOIs, neuroleptics
With carbamazepine: not recommended — less analgesia and added seizure risk
In overdose, naloxone may increase seizure risk
Beers 2023 (≥65): reduce IR dose and avoid ER at CrCl <30
Label on file is the 2010 Ultram ER label
sources: Ultram ER (tramadol HCl) extended-release tablets US prescribing information (Rebel Distributors); revised 12/2010 (user-supplied label)

2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc 2023;71:2052-2081. doi:10.1111/jgs.18372

entries.title: Meperidine
effect: Seizures with or without a seizure disorder; prolonged use and renal impairment accumulate the neurotoxic metabolite normeperidine
pearls: Label: monitor seizure control in patients with epilepsy; titrate slowly and watch for CNS toxicity in renal impairment
Contraindicated with MAOIs or within 14 days of stopping one
Beers 2023 (≥65): avoid — neurotoxicity including delirium; safer alternatives exist
sources: Demerol (meperidine hydrochloride) injection US prescribing information. Hospira; revised 12/2025 (user-supplied label)

2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc 2023;71:2052-2081. doi:10.1111/jgs.18372

entries.title: Isoniazid
effect: Convulsions uncommon at conventional doses; overdose → severe, intractable seizures, coma and severe metabolic acidosis within 30 min–3 h
pearls: Gross overdose 80–150 mg/kg can be fatal; acute ingestion >80 mg/kg gets IV pyridoxine even if asymptomatic
Pyridoxine IV gram for gram equal to the isoniazid dose; amount unknown: 5 g (adult)
Symptomatic: give pyridoxine as a slow IV bolus over 3–5 min; asymptomatic with unknown amount: 5 g over 30–60 min
Seizures continue: repeat pyridoxine (rarely >10 g; maximum safe dose unknown); no response: diazepam
Phenytoin only with caution — isoniazid inhibits its metabolism
Isoniazid raises carbamazepine and phenytoin levels — check a carbamazepine level before starting; adjust the ASM dose
sources: Isoniazid tablets USP US prescribing information. Marlex; revised 9/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Imipenem-cilastatin
effect: Seizures 0.4% in adult trials; also confusion and myoclonus — mostly with CNS disorders (brain lesions, prior seizures), renal impairment or above-recommended doses
pearls: CrCl ≤30 mL/min, with or without hemodialysis: higher seizure risk — dose strictly to renal function (§2.3, §8.6)
CrCl <15 mL/min: don't give unless hemodialysis starts within 48 h; on hemodialysis only if benefit outweighs seizure risk (§2.3–2.4)
Focal tremor, myoclonus or seizure: evaluate, start an ASM if not on one, and reduce the dose or stop (§5.2)
Ganciclovir: generalized seizures reported — avoid together unless benefit outweighs risk (§7.1)
Valproate: generally not recommended — see asm-interactions (§5.3)
sources: Primaxin (imipenem and cilastatin) for injection US prescribing information. Merck Sharp & Dohme; revised 7/2024 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine
effect: Tacrolimus: PRES, delirium, seizures and coma; also tremor, paresthesias, headache — linked to troughs at or above range (Prograf §5.6)
Cyclosporine: convulsions, especially with high-dose methylprednisolone; encephalopathy including PRES (Neoral Warnings)
pearls: Tacrolimus neurotoxicity: check the trough; consider dose reduction or stopping (Prograf §5.6)
Cyclosporine PRES risk factors: hypertension, hypomagnesemia, hypocholesterolemia, high-dose steroids, high cyclosporine levels, GVHD; liver > kidney transplant (Neoral Warnings)
Cyclosporine encephalopathy usually reverses after stopping; some improve with dose reduction (Neoral Warnings)
Cyclosporine: rare optic disc edema/papilledema from intracranial hypertension (Neoral Warnings)
Strong CYP3A inhibitors (voriconazole, posaconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir): rapid, sharp tacrolimus rise despite dose reduction — neurotoxicity risk (Prograf §5.11, Table 15)
Enzyme-inducing ASMs lower both drugs' levels — see asm-interactions
sources: Prograf (tacrolimus) capsules, injection, granules US prescribing information. Astellas; revised 8/2023 (user-supplied label)
Neoral (cyclosporine) capsules and oral solution (modified) US prescribing information. Novartis; revised 8/2026 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Ifosfamide
effect: Encephalopathy, sometimes fatal: confusion, somnolence, coma, hallucinations, extrapyramidal signs, seizures; onset hours to days after a dose and may recur (§5.2)
pearls: Boxed warning: encephalopathy (seizures are among its signs, §5.2)
Risk factors: high dose, hypoalbuminemia, renal impairment, poor performance status, bulky abdominal-pelvic disease, nephrotoxic drugs incl. cisplatin, CNS-active drugs, alcohol (§5.2)
Label: consider methylene blue for encephalopathy — no dose given (§5.2)
CYP3A4 inducers may increase chloroacetaldehyde, the neurotoxic metabolite — monitor for toxicity (§7.1)
Rechallenge after neurotoxicity: some recurred, including fatal events (§6.2)
sources: Ifex (ifosfamide) for injection US prescribing information. Baxter; revised 10/2026 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Intrathecal baclofen — abrupt withdrawal or overdose
effect: Seizures with withdrawal, with overdose, and at therapeutic doses (Gablofen §5.5)
Convulsion on maintenance infusion: 4.7% (spinal origin), 10.0% (cerebral origin) in trials (Gablofen §6.1, Tables 1–2)
pearls: AVOID = avoid abrupt interruption (boxed warning: "Do not discontinue abruptly")
Abrupt stop → high fever, altered mental status, rebound spasticity, rigidity; rarely rhabdomyolysis, multiorgan failure, death (boxed warning)
Early withdrawal: return of spasticity, pruritus, hypotension, paresthesias; onset hours to a few days (§5.5)
Advanced withdrawal can resemble autonomic dysreflexia, sepsis, malignant hyperthermia or NMS (§5.5)
Common causes: catheter malfunction (especially disconnection), low reservoir volume, pump battery end of life (§5.5)
Higher risk: spinal cord injury at T6 or above, communication difficulties, prior withdrawal (boxed warning)
Treat withdrawal: restore intrathecal baclofen at or near the prior dose; if delayed, oral/enteral baclofen or oral/enteral/IV benzodiazepines — oral baclofen alone isn't enough (§5.5)
Overdose: drowsiness, respiratory depression, seizures, rostral hypotonia, coma up to 72 h; no antidote — remove residual drug from the pump, intubate if needed (§10)
Overdose: physostigmine 2 mg IM/IV at ≤1 mg/min may reverse drowsiness and respiratory depression (anecdotal), but can induce seizures and bradycardia (§10)
Overdose: if LP not contraindicated, consider withdrawing 30–40 mL CSF (§10)
sources: Gablofen (baclofen injection) intrathecal US prescribing information. Piramal Critical Care; revised 5/2026 (user-supplied label)
Lioresal Intrathecal (baclofen injection) US prescribing information. Amneal; revised 12/2022 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Busulfan (high-dose IV conditioning)
effect: Seizures with high-dose busulfan; 1/42 seized despite phenytoin prophylaxis, 36 h after the last dose (§5.2)
pearls: Label requires ASM prophylaxis: start 12 h before the first dose and continue to 24 h after the last (§2.1)
Label options: benzodiazepines, phenytoin, valproic acid or levetiracetam (§2.1, §5.2)
Phenytoin ↑ busulfan clearance ≥15%; label PK was studied on phenytoin, so exposure may be higher without it (§7.2)
Use caution with prior seizures, head trauma or other epileptogenic drugs (§5.2)
sources: Busulfex (busulfan) injection US prescribing information. Otsuka; revised 10/2026 (user-supplied label)
